title: How Casey Adams went from a neck brace to a MediaKits exit at 26 and built Listener
summary: Casey Adams explains how podcasting from age 17 became the foundation for his network, his first raise ($1.5M from 37 angels, mostly past guests) and his MediaKits exit to Viral Nation. He then shares lessons from that exit and how he keeps his second company, Listener, lean while preserving optionality.

principles.text: Be crystal clear on why you do a hard medium like podcasting; clarity makes it stop feeling like a heavy lift.
principles.quote: know why you're doing it. It's a hard medium. There's a lot of in, you know, long format. It's hard to get attention. It's hard to build that like true listener base. But if you're clear with why you're doing it, it should never feel like that heavy lift.

principles.text: Use a podcast as a network engine: guests can become your investors, introducers and strategic partners.
principles.quote: we ended up raising, you know, $1.5 million from 37 angel investors. And you'll love this and then I'll I'll pause for a moment. Pretty much all of those 37 angel investors were past guests on my podcast.

principles.text: Do the reps before the opportunity: volume of interviews prepared him for the Larry King chance.
principles.quote: the butterfly effect of like those 60 or 100 interviews that I did beforehand is what gave me that opportunity to be prepared for that opportunity.

principles.text: Stay narrow: be an inch wide and a mile deep, doing one thing great rather than many things okay.
principles.quote: We were an inch wide and a mile deep. Like our name was media kits.com. The easiest way to build a media kit.

principles.text: Take an early exit when the future is uncertain; a win on the board proves you can run the full lifecycle and is reusable.
principles.quote: for us it was like getting a great win on the board and being able to utilize that into future ventures.

principles.text: Stay lean and keep optionality: don't over-raise before you've figured out the product, so you can raise, grow sustainably, or be acquired.
principles.quote: give yourself the ability to have optionality like we have great investors and the option to if we wanted to go raise a like prop around.
